title: The Box That Waited
synopsis: A girl's box is lost in a busy office in Chongqing.
Her mother said: open it on the day the war is over.
goal: Find Bitna's mother's box and open its lock on the right day.

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene) of the government office: Father's note on the desk is read first, then the three trunks by the wall. Each wrong trunk shares one thing with the right one (a round brass lock, or one strap): the strap count and the lock together decide.

lines.text: Welcome, Detective. The war may end soon, so we pack our papers.
Bitna's father packed her mother's box with them, by mistake.
He went home to the little ones. He left a note on the desk.
Then I will find that note.

notes: Mother's letters (made up) are ordered by her own lines: the rain letter says it came after the pine letter, and the moon letter says the rain is over. The first letter (April) is fixed. The drawing is not a letter and is set aside.
The cards are listed rain, drawing, first, moon, pine: never in the answer's order (the board does not shuffle).

play.title: Mother's Letters
story: You carry the box to Bitna's room. Her father and brothers are there.
Her little brother opens the top. Mother's letters fall out.
"Mother sends a letter when she can," Bitna says.
play.letter:
First letter (April): "I go to the Liberation Army today. I will write to you."
"My riddle is on the backs, one piece on each. Only the right order makes sense."
Pine letter: "I am far away now. There are pine trees on the hill."
Rain letter: "After my pine letter, the rain came. My boots are wet."
Moon letter: "The rain is over now. The moon is bright tonight."
play.question: Put Mother's letters in order, from the first.
hints: The first letter has its month on it. Now read the rain letter.
The moon letter says the rain is over. So it came after the rain letter.
play.successMessage: Mother's letters are back in order!
transition: You turn them over, in order. The pieces join into one riddle.
"The sun gives it." "At night, it goes away."
"It comes back on the day the war is over." "'May' is not enough."
play.orderFeedback: Read the rain letter and the moon letter again. Which came first?

notes: Mother's lock: seven tiles N, H, T, I, R, G, L (listed so they never spell the answer), five of them spell LIGHT, read in Mother's riddle on the backs of her letters (the sun gives it; at night, it goes away; it comes back on the day the war is over). N and R are extra: NIGHT, RIGHT, THING, GLINT and GIRTH can be made too, and each has its own line pointing back to the riddle. What gwang (光) means in gwangbok, the light comes back (h5), is told in the ending.
PART 1.5 (engine 2a, decoy tiles): the lock has a slot for each letter of LIGHT; the two extra tiles stay on the desk.
Liberation is never one person's work: the ending says the Allies won the war and many Koreans, at home and far away, worked for it (h3, h4).

learningGoal.title: Reading clues, order, dates and the meaning of gwangbok

objectives: Find the day the lock can open.
intro: August, 1945. You are a guest of Korea's government in Chongqing, China.
Japan has ruled Korea since 1910. So this government works far from home.
Kim Won-bong, the government's minister for the army, meets you at the door.
A girl runs up to you: "I am Bitna. My mother's box is lost!"
"Mother said: open its lock only on the day the war is over."
play.caseSummary: Bitna's mother left her a box with a word lock. Open it on the day the war is over, she said. 'May' is not enough. Bitna's father packed it in a trunk by mistake. On 15 August 1945, Japan gave up and the war was over. Bitna opened the lock with Mother's word: LIGHT. Inside was the flag Mother sewed. In Korean, this day is gwangbok: the light comes back. The Allies won the war, and many Koreans worked for this day.

notes: Season 5 Case 12, a standalone case (PART 1B, 2026-11-09): Bitna's mother's box, lost in the office, is opened on the day the war is over. Kim Won-bong is real (minister of military affairs of the Provisional Government from 1944, h2); everything he says and does here is made up. His life after 1945 is outside the case and never told.

Bitna, her mother, father and brothers, Mother's letters and the lines on their backs, the box, its lock and tiles, the flag, the trunks, Father's note, the date card and the radio's words are made up. No other case's people, notes or evidence appear.

The case ends on checked facts: Japan's surrender announced on the radio on 15 August 1945 (h3, h10), liberation from the Allied victory and many Koreans' work (h4), the Liberation Army's plan called off (h6), and gwangbok meaning 'the light comes back' (h5).
